subject: put a prior on just two inferred parameters

messages.author: 7a97c986864bf6d6
messages.subject: put a prior on just two inferred parameters
parts:
Hello Community,

I have a regression model. In my design instead of inferring angular coefficient with many points, I do the other way around (a point called GAMMA with many angular coefficients).

Said that my problem can be reduces to this:

If I predict gamma[1] and gamma[2] from two independent datasets, but I know they should be "linked" to the same distribution. so I put gamma ~ normal(mu, sigma)

The problem that two points are not enough to calculate a normal distribution. And there is not convergence.

Does this make sense? Is it something illogical to do?

Thanks

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] put a prior on just two inferred parameters
parts:
> On Feb 16, 2017, at 6:36 PM, Stefano <mangiol...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hello Community,
>
> I have a regression model. In my design instead of inferring angular coefficient with many points, I do the other way around (a point called GAMMA with many angular coefficients).
>
> Said that my problem can be reduces to this:
>
> If I predict gamma[1] and gamma[2] from two independent datasets, but I know they should be "linked" to the same distribution. so I put gamma ~ normal(mu, sigma)

I don't know what you mean by predict or linked, but I understand the
Stan sampling statement.
> The problem that two points are not enough to calculate a normal distribution. And there is not convergence.

Put a proper prior on mu and sigma and then you'll get a proper
posterior and shouldn't have convergence issues. Cauchy prior
may still be too fat.

>
> Does this make sense? Is it something illogical to do?

It's more useful in a hierarchical modeling setting where there
are other groups from which to estimate hyper-priors.

- Bob
